jobs.title: Director, FP&A
jobs.description:
At Range Group
we believe in the power of the professional travel advisor. We represent over $4.5 billion in annual travel sales. All our investments stem from a common thesis, that travel advisors add real value to a trip. Travel advisors when equipped with technology and 24/7 support are irreplaceable. Equally important is our philanthropy. Range Foundation channels 10% of group profits to social impact. From exploration grants, improved access to education, new discoveries on sea and land, cultural infrastructure, and helping our global neighbors in times of need — we are investing to build a better future.

About The Role

This is a hands-on senior finance leadership role for someone who operates at the intersection of strategy, analytics, and execution. You’re as comfortable building a complex multi-entity model from scratch as you are presenting the story behind the numbers to the executive team.

As Director, FP&A, you will own the analytical engine that supports decision-making across Range Group’s portfolio of travel brands — leading enterprise planning and forecasting, managing a small team, and working directly with senior leadership to evaluate opportunities, navigate risks, and drive performance.

What You’ll Do

Financial Modelling & Planning

Build, maintain, and continuously improve financial models covering consolidated Group performance, brand-level P&Ls, cash flow forecasting, and scenario analysis.
Own the Group-level cash flow tracker and EBITDA bridging model, ensuring accuracy and timeliness week over week.
Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes across the organization.
Support ad hoc financial analysis — acquisition modelling, business case development, and covenant compliance.
Drive continuous improvement in financial planning frameworks, forecasting methodologies, and analytical tools.

Performance Management & Executive Insights

Own enterprise-wide performance reporting — financial reviews, KPI dashboards, executive scorecards, and variance commentary.
Lead monthly and quarterly business reviews with senior leadership.
Translate financial results into clear, decision-ready insights that prompt action.
Identify and proactively flag emerging risks, opportunities, and performance trends across the portfolio.

Strategic Business Partnership

Partner with executive and business leaders to align financial plans with strategic priorities and growth objectives.
Evaluate investments, business initiatives, and strategic opportunities through modelling and scenario analysis.
Provide financial leadership on strategic initiatives, business cases, and investment decisions.
Support executive and Board reporting requirements.

Treasury & Foreign Exchange Management

Own foreign exchange exposure tracking, reporting, and scenario analysis across the Group's multi-currency operations.
Partner with treasury, banking partners, and external advisors to evaluate foreign exchange risks and mitigation strategies.
Assess the financial impact of currency fluctuations on forecasts, budgets, cash flow, and business performance.
Develop recommendations and decision-support materials for leadership regarding FX risk management and capital planning.
Monitor market trends and currency movements, proactively identifying risks and opportunities that may impact business performance.

Team Leadership & Capability Building

Lead a small finance team — including a Finance Manager and intern — as a player-coach: owning models and analysis end-to-end while delegating and developing where appropriate.
Foster a high-performance, analytically rigorous culture within the team.
Support ERP and reporting tool improvements from a finance data and output perspective.
Champion the evolution of finance from a reporting function to a true strategic business partner.

What You’ll Bring

8+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, Corporate Finance, Strategic Finance, or Finance Business Partnering — with a track record of owning complex models in a multi-entity environment.
Advanced Excel skills — non-negotiable. You build models from scratch, structure them for auditability, and are fast and precise in the tool.
Strong accounting foundation: you understand how the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement connect inside a model.
Proven experience leading enterprise budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes.
Experience analyzing foreign exchange exposure, multi-currency financial impacts, and scenario modelling within a corporate FP&A, finance, or strategic finance environment.
Strong executive presence, comfortable presenting to senior leadership and capable of influencing and constructively challenging stakeholders.
Experience in multi-entity and multi-currency operating environments.
CPA designation strongly preferred; candidates without the designation will be considered where technical skills and experience are strong.
Background in travel, technology, hospitality, or another fast-paced, multi-brand environment is an asset.

Who You Are

You are a builder. You prefer to own models end-to-end and take pride in work that is structured, auditable, and built to last.
You are intellectually curious and detail-oriented, but able to zoom out and connect the numbers to a broader business narrative.
You operate well with ambiguity and can manage competing priorities without losing accuracy or composure.
You are a collaborative leader who still wants to be close to the work — energized by doing, not just directing.
You communicate with a low-ego, peer-level style — credible with senior stakeholders, collegial with the broader team, and proactive about surfacing issues.

Why Join Range Group

This is a rare opportunity to bridge corporate finance and executive strategy in a multi-brand travel and technology portfolio. You’ll have genuine influence — shaping how capital is allocated, how performance is communicated, and how the finance function evolves as the company grows.

The role carries real complexity: multi-entity consolidations, multi-currency exposure, and a direct reporting line to the Chief Finance Officer. You’ll lead a small team and have the space to build the frameworks and processes that become the foundation for the company’s next phase.

Hybrid Work Model

We’re based in Toronto and targeting three days in office per week, with flexibility built in.

We provide a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. Employees have the opportunity to participate in incentive programs and compensation tied to business and individual performance. The actual compensation may vary depending on local market conditions, geography and relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience, and education/training.

We are committed to providing employment accommodation in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. If you require accommodation due to a disability at any stage of our hiring process, please advise us when completing your application.

The Range Group may use artificial intelligence throughout the recruitment process to screen, assess or select applicants for this position. These tools assist our hiring team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans.

We thank all candidates for their interest however only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Associate director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Associate Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, you will head the Financial Planning & Analysis team at Novo Canada. You will own the budgeting of ex-factory sales and costs, manage operating profit and guide how resources are allocated, giving the President, CFO and Executive Team the clarity to decide and act. Your work helps the affiliate reach its financial and strategic goals and keeps our products available to the people who rely on them.

What You’ll Bring

You combine strong financial expertise with the leadership to build a high-performing team.

You Will Also Bring

A bachelor/master’s degree in business administration, finance, business economics, accounting or auditing.
At least 5 years of experience in finance, with proven success in numbers-driven analysis, planning and reporting.
Experience presenting to senior management and executives, and the ability to explain quantitative analysis clearly.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and a track record of planning, prioritising and following through while proactively managing risks.
A proven track record in complex, cross-affiliate project management.
An understanding of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and internal controls.
Proficiency in SAP, Business Warehouse and Excel.
In-depth understanding of the global budgeting process at Novo or a company of similar size.
A leadership style that builds trust, gives honest feedback, sets clear priorities and keeps things simple, especially through change.

What You’ll Do

You will lead the full financial planning cycle for Novo Canada and the commercial terms that connect our products to customers.

Your Work Will Help To

Lead, develop and plan the work of the Financial Planning & Analysis team, including hiring, succession, individual development plans and performance dialogue, and manage the team budget.
Oversee the affiliate P&L, including ex-factory sales, cost of goods sold and total operating costs, and own the total ex-factory sales forecast and targets.
Run the annual budget and rolling estimate processes, challenging submissions, ensuring compliance with corporate guidelines and anchoring approved targets across the business, while advising the President and CFO on resource allocation and supporting the Executive Team’s cost target.
Deliver monthly and quarterly reporting to management, the region and headquarters on sales, expenses and operating profit, flagging issues early and proposing corrective actions.
Own gross-to-net including rebate accruals under provincial Product Listing Agreements, and weekly sales performance reporting.
Lead priority initiatives for Financial Planning & Analysis and contribute to value-creation projects across Executive Team areas, and work with other affiliates to share best practices and keep planning simple and value-adding.

Who You’ll Work With

You will join Finance & Operations at Novo Canada as a member of the Finance & Operations Leadership Team. You will lead the Financial Planning & Analysis team, which you will help shape and grow.

Your closest partners will be the President, the CFO and the Executive Team. You will bring a financial perspective to the commercial teams, joining their management meetings, and support Line of Business colleagues with managing investments, month-end closing and training on financial processes.

You will also work with regional finance, headquarters, the Pricing Committee and colleagues in other affiliates, and directly with buyers at key wholesalers. These relationships let you turn numbers into clear, timely decisions.

What You Can Expect Here

You will take on a leadership role where your voice shapes decisions at executive level. The role gives you a broad view of the business, from budgets and operating profit to trade strategy, pricing and launches, and the opportunity to build new skills through cross-functional and cross-affiliate work.
You will be trusted to own your area and make decisions, with clear performance expectations and a culture that rewards results. You will also help your team thrive and grow through coaching, development plans and ongoing dialogue about performance and development.

What We Offer

At Novo, you'll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

Job Description

As a Project Controls Director, you will lead multidisciplinary teams, advise clients on complex project and program challenges, and provide strategic oversight across the full project lifecycle, from planning and procurement through construction and handover. You will play a key role in fostering high-performing teams, enhancing client relationships, and driving best practices in project controls across large-scale real estate and infrastructure programs.

Raymond James Ltd. is Canada’s leading independent investment dealers offering high quality investment products and services to Canadians seeking customized solutions to their wealth management needs.

Vice President, Controller

How does the role impact the organization?

The Vice President, Controller is a senior finance leader responsible for the integrity of the organization’s financial records, consolidated financial statements, regulatory reporting, accounting policies, controls, and core accounting operations. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the role provides trusted advice to executive leadership, ensures compliance with applicable accounting tax and regulatory requirements, and builds scalable processes that support accurate, timely, and decision-useful financial information. The Vice President, Controller leads the financial reporting team and promotes accountability, operational discipline, sound risk management, inter-departmental teamwork, service excellence and continuous improvement.

What will your role be responsible for?

Controllership and Executive Leadership

Serve as the organization’s authority on accounting, financial reporting, corporate tax and controllership matters.
Advise the Chief Financial Officer and executive leadership on accounting conclusions, reporting risks, control matters, and regulatory developments.
Establish the operating model, service standards, and priorities in alignment with enterprise objectives.
Provide clear, balanced recommendations on complex transactions, organizational initiatives, and matters affecting financial integrity.

Financial Reporting and Close

Lead accurate and timely monthly, quarterly, and annual close, consolidation, and financial statement preparation.
Ensure financial reporting complies with IFRS, applicable U.S. GAAP requirements, corporate policies, and disclosure obligations.
Own accounting policies and conclusions for complex, unusual, or significant transactions, ensuring decisions are appropriately documented.
Provide executive and governance reporting that clearly explains financial results, material judgements, emerging issues, and required actions.

Regulatory Reporting and Capital Compliance

Oversee complete, accurate, and timely regulatory reporting and regulatory capital calculations for the organization and applicable subsidiaries.
Maintain current knowledge of CIRO requirements and, where applicable, FINRA, OSFI, CSA , and other regulatory obligations.
Establish effective review, certification, escalation, and evidence-retention processes for regulatory submissions.
Monitor capital, liquidity, and reporting risks and advise leadership promptly on emerging requirements, issues, or potential breaches.

Internal Controls, Audit, and Compliance

Design, maintain, and continuously improve the internal control framework over financial and regulatory reporting.
Safeguard the integrity of the general ledger, reconciliations, financial systems, and supporting data through clear ownership and effective review controls.
Lead relationships with internal and external auditors, coordinate audit deliverables, and ensure findings are resolved appropriately and on time.
Promote compliance with legal, regulatory, tax, accounting, and corporate policy requirements while ensuring material issues are transparently escalated.

Accounting Operations and Finance Transformation

Oversee accurate and timely monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting in accordance with applicable accounting standards and organizational requirements.
Maintain effective close, consolidation reconciliation, and reporting processes.
Ensure financial data, policies procedures and records are complete, consistent, secure and audit ready.
Ensure finance systems, the chart of accounts, data flows, and reporting structures support reliable consolidation, analysis, and regulatory reporting.
Lead process simplification, standardization, automation, and responsible adoption of emerging technologies to improve timeliness, accuracy, and scalability.
Partner with, Private Client & Equity Capital Markets Leadership, Treasury, Risk, Operations, Technology, and other functions to support business decisions, transactions, integrations, and enterprise initiatives.

People Leadership

Build, lead, and retain a high-performing finance team with strong technical, operational, and business-partnering capabilities.
Set clear expectations, decision rights, service standards, and accountabilities across the function.
Coach and develop leaders, maintain succession plans, and build capacity for evolving reporting, regulatory, and technology requirements.
Foster an inclusive culture grounded in integrity, professional judgement, service excellence, constructive challenge, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

What can you expect from us?

Our most important investment is in people. Upon eligibility, Raymond James Ltd offers flexible workstyles,
a competitive compensation and benefits package. Our benefits range from Health Benefits, RRSP Matching Program, Employee Stock Purchase Plan, Paid Time Off, Volunteer Days, Discretionary Bonuses, Tuition Reimbursement and many more! We also support internal promotion and community involvement.

What do we expect from you?

Minimum 10 years progressive accounting and controllership experience, including leadership responsibility for financial reporting, accounting operations, controls, and audit
Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, commerce, business administration, or a related discipline.
Canadian Chartered Professional Accountant designation or an equivalent recognized professional accounting designation is required.
Willingness to complete CIRO Directors & Executive exam or equivalent within 1 year of employment.
Completion or intention to complete CIRO CFO exam.
Advanced technical knowledge of IFRS experience assessing and documenting complex accounting matters.
Experience in a regulated financial services environment, including regulatory reporting and capital requirements, is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated boardroom experience advising senior executives and presenting financial, results , analysis and risk related matters to executive or governance audiences.
Proven success leading and developing teams, strengthening internal controls, improving close processes, and implementing finance systems or automation.
Experience with multi-entity consolidation, US-Canada cross-border operations, tax, treasury, and working knowledge of U.S. GAAP; and significant transactions is an asset.
Work experience in a Big 4 Accounting firm is an asset.
Completion of Finra series 27 exam is an asset.

Leadership Competencies

Strategic perspective: Connects financial insight to enterprise priorities and long-term outcomes.
Financial and business acumen: Applies rigorous analysis and commercial judgement to complex decisions.
Executive communication: Presents clear, concise, and credible advice to senior stakeholders.
Enterprise collaboration: Builds trust across functions and constructively influences decisions.
Risk and control mindset: Balances business agility with disciplined governance and accountability.
Change leadership: Leads transformation with clarity, resilience, and a focus on sustainable adoption.
People leadership: Creates an inclusive environment that develops talent and enables strong performance.
Integrity: Demonstrates discretion, objectivity, and consistently high ethical standards.

Working Conditions

Works in-office 4-5 days per week
Requires occasional travel and availability outside standard business hours during reporting cycles, audits, transactions, or other critical business periods.
Handles confidential, sensitive, and material financial information with a high degree of discretion.

Grow professionally and inspire others to do the same
Work with and through others to achieve desired outcomes
Make prompt, pragmatic choices and act with the client in mind
Take ownership and hold themselves and others accountable for delivering results that matter
Contribute to the continuous evolution of the firm

jobs.description:
About Us

Embrace Software acquires mission-critical businesses and helps them thrive for the long term. With 17+ acquisitions across healthcare, industrial, financial services, education, legal, and public sector, our portfolio runs inside 16% of the Fortune 500, 45+ state agencies, and 450+ banks and credit unions. We don’t flip companies; we keep them, invest in them, and rebuild them around AI, while our Venture Lab launches new AI-native products into the same markets. Named to the Inc. 5000 list of America’s Fastest-Growing Private Companies and an 8x Top Workplaces award winner, Embrace brings together top talent from around the world to build lasting products, own real outcomes, and grow with a company that plays the long game.

Job Description

This is a remote position.

Role Overview

This is an opportunity to work directly with the CEO of Embrace as Chief of Staff, leading strategic and high-impact operational projects across the portfolio, from growing and optimising businesses to strategy. You will work closely with portfolio company CEOs and the Operating Leaders across our industry groups.

Core Mandate

Partner with the CEO on strategic and high-impact operational priorities
Grow and optimize portfolio companies, applying and building Embrace's value creation playbooks
Scale AI and operating best practices across the portfolio for measurable ROI
Build the experience to take on senior leadership in the portfolio

Key Responsibilities

1. Grow & Optimize

Lead growth work with portfolio CEOs on pricing, go-to-market, and retention.
Diagnose underperformance and reset cost structure, organization, and cash flow.
Use AI and data to sharpen diagnostics on churn risk, pricing, and cost benchmarks.
Set clear KPIs for each initiative and turn what works into repeatable playbooks.

2. Portfolio Operations & AI Transformation

Set a consistent operating cadence and KPI dashboards across the portfolio.
Drive end-to-end AI automation across product, services, and internal workflows.
Prioritize AI use cases by ROI, track adoption, and build AI fluency across teams.

3. Strategy & Office of the CEO

Support corporate strategy, annual planning, and board and investor materials.
Run the leadership team's operating rhythm and lead special projects for the CEO.

4. Change Management

Lead the people side of transformation, including restructurings, leadership transitions, underperformance, and resistance to change.
Handle difficult conversations with fairness, discretion, and maturity.
Build trust with portfolio CEOs, Operating Leaders, and functional leaders.

How You'll Spend Your Time

Operations, including growth, optimization, and portfolio performance (~80%); strategy and the Office of the CEO (~20%).

Path to Leadership

You will work closely with the CEO and be mentored by Embrace's Operating Leaders. High performers will have the opportunity to move into senior leadership roles across the portfolio, with the long-term goal of leading an Embrace company as CEO.

What Success Looks Like (18–24 Months)

Measurable revenue growth and EBITDA improvement in the companies you support.
AI live in core workflows, with measurable productivity and ROI gains.
Growth and productivity playbooks driven hands-on at portfolio companies.
Short feedback loops and fast iteration on every initiative.
Change led while keeping key talent and the trust of teams and customers.
Ready to take on a senior leadership role in the portfolio.

Requirements

Ideal Candidate Profile

8+ years of progressive experience across operating roles, management consulting, or private equity operations, including hands-on operating leadership roles.
Grew and improved software/SaaS businesses, ideally with P&L or departmental-level ownership.
Proven experience managing difficult people situations during transformations and restructuring, with the maturity and presence to earn trust through change.
Strong analytical and financial skills: P&Ls, models, and business cases.
Applied AI and automation to business workflows, with measurable results.
A long-term ambition to run a company. An MBA from a top program is a plus.

Nice to Have

Industry experience in financial services, healthcare, legal, or manufacturing.
Buy-and-hold software acquirer, holdco, start-up, Series A/B scale-up, or PE-backed experience is a strong asset.

Strengthen the security resilience of one of the few environments where research, clinical care, and hospital operations converge. As a Director, Cybersecurity
at Sinai Health, you will lead the tactical and operational work needed to turn an established security roadmap into lasting safeguards. This is a hands-on leadership role where you actively steer risk assessments, security operations, and technical controls alongside team members and external partners. You will pair advanced security tooling and industry-leading partners to protect corporate systems, health services, personal information (PI), personal health information (PHI), research data and intellectual property. Few sectors face the scale, complexity and potential consequences of cyber threats that healthcare does. Your work keeps those systems safe preserving the trust of the communities we serve.

Is this you?

Bringing people together around a shared goal is how you advance risk posture across complex environments. Cybersecurity is a shared responsibility that no single team can carry alone, so the relationships you build matter as much as the controls you put in place. Working in close collaboration with IT, privacy, clinical, and corporate teams allows you to apply security controls in ways that support everyday work. Whether you are shaping a new policy or rolling out a control, you build support across teams by showing how it protects the work they already care about. The shared ownership you cultivate helps a culture of security take root across the organization.

Are you proactive about keeping current about new technologies and emerging threats? This field moves quickly, so staying effective means understanding what’s trending and what it means for the systems you protect. Industry research, threat intelligence, and strong partner relationships keep you informed about where the field is heading. Whether you are evaluating a new tool or a vendor’s latest offering, you weigh the investment against the organization’s needs and priorities to ensure it’s the right use of our investments and time. The knowledge you build keeps the organization ahead of emerging threats and keeps you growing as a professional.

A practical command of security technology gives you a clear understanding of how systems behave. This is a role where you work with the systems yourself, so your knowledge stays current and applied. Whether you are reviewing how access is configured in the Epic electronic health record platform or tuning the detection rules behind your monitoring, you are at ease working in the technology directly. This is where deep technical skill and senior leadership reinforce each other, keeping you engaged with the technology on a daily basis.

Strong problem-solving skills are essential in a role like this, where the decisions you face rarely come with an obvious answer. This position sits at the point where business priorities and technical demands converge, requiring someone with the confidence and critical thinking to arrive at solutions that work for both. The impact of your judgment extends well beyond the security team, shapes outcomes that matter across the whole organization, making your work widely visible.

In This Role You Will

Lead the development and maintenance of information security policies and standards, owning and maintaining the enterprise cyber risk register and governance framework
Lead compliance activities under PHIPA and the Ontario Cyber Security Framework/Regulation, coordinating evidence collection, control testing, and gap remediation
Integrate cyber governance, risk, and compliance activities with other hospital risk management and advisory functions, including Enterprise Risk Management, Privacy, Legal, and Internal Audit, to ensure a coordinated approach to risk, incident response, and regulatory obligations
Prepare and present risk and compliance reporting for various committees, senior leadership, and internal/external auditors
Lead third-party risk assessments from a governance perspective, including privacy and contractual risk considerations, in partnership with Procurement, Privacy, and Legal
Own and mature the cyber threat and vulnerability risk management program, including threat intelligence, threat management tools and risk-mitigation processes
Direct prioritization, tracking, and reporting of vulnerability and threat remediation across endpoints, servers, network, and cloud/SaaS environments
Own selection, configuration, and lifecycle management of risk management tooling (e.g., GRC platform, vulnerability management, threat intelligence feeds)
Lead risk assessments for new systems, vendors, and technology changes, and maintain associated risk treatment plans
Conduct direct day-to-day security operations, including SIEM/SOC monitoring, detection, and incident response, delivered through internal staff and managed security service providers
Own the incident response process end-to-end: triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident/lessons-learned review
Direct endpoint security strategy (EDR/anti-malware, hardening baselines) and identity/access security operations, including Cloud Identity Services federation, Epic EHR access, and Microsoft 365/Entra ID security
Coordinate vendor-delivered assessments (penetration tests, tabletop exercises) and ensure findings are integrated into the risk register
Supervise direct reports (e.g., Cyber Security Analyst and IAM/Operations Analyst), including performance management, coaching, and development planning
Perform other duties consistent with the job classification as required

Mandatory

7 years of related experience in a cybersecurity leadership position
College Diploma or bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Security, or a related technical field

Preferred

Previous experience in a clinical or hospital environment

Skills and Knowledge

Expert knowledge of cyber security frameworks and standards (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls) and Ontario health-sector requirements (PHIPA, Ontario Cyber Security Framework/Regulation)
Expert working knowledge of security operations tooling: SIEM, EDR/endpoint protection, vulnerability management, and MSSP/MDR service models

People leadership and coaching skills

Strengthen the security resilience of one of the few environments where research, clinical care, and hospital operations converge. As a Director, Cybersecurity
at Sinai Health, you will lead the tactical and operational work needed to turn an established security roadmap into lasting safeguards. This is a hands-on leadership role where you actively steer risk assessments, security operations, and technical controls alongside team members and external partners. You will pair advanced security tooling and industry-leading partners to protect corporate systems, health services, personal information (PI), personal health information (PHI), research data and intellectual property. Few sectors face the scale, complexity and potential consequences of cyber threats that healthcare does. Your work keeps those systems safe preserving the trust of the communities we serve.

Is this you?

Bringing people together around a shared goal is how you advance risk posture across complex environments. Cybersecurity is a shared responsibility that no single team can carry alone, so the relationships you build matter as much as the controls you put in place. Working in close collaboration with IT, privacy, clinical, and corporate teams allows you to apply security controls in ways that support everyday work. Whether you are shaping a new policy or rolling out a control, you build support across teams by showing how it protects the work they already care about. The shared ownership you cultivate helps a culture of security take root across the organization.

Are you proactive about keeping current about new technologies and emerging threats? This field moves quickly, so staying effective means understanding what’s trending and what it means for the systems you protect. Industry research, threat intelligence, and strong partner relationships keep you informed about where the field is heading. Whether you are evaluating a new tool or a vendor’s latest offering, you weigh the investment against the organization’s needs and priorities to ensure it’s the right use of our investments and time. The knowledge you build keeps the organization ahead of emerging threats and keeps you growing as a professional.

A practical command of security technology gives you a clear understanding of how systems behave. This is a role where you work with the systems yourself, so your knowledge stays current and applied. Whether you are reviewing how access is configured in the Epic electronic health record platform or tuning the detection rules behind your monitoring, you are at ease working in the technology directly. This is where deep technical skill and senior leadership reinforce each other, keeping you engaged with the technology on a daily basis.

Strong problem-solving skills are essential in a role like this, where the decisions you face rarely come with an obvious answer. This position sits at the point where business priorities and technical demands converge, requiring someone with the confidence and critical thinking to arrive at solutions that work for both. The impact of your judgment extends well beyond the security team, shapes outcomes that matter across the whole organization, making your work widely visible.

In This Role You Will

Lead the development and maintenance of information security policies and standards, owning and maintaining the enterprise cyber risk register and governance framework
Lead compliance activities under PHIPA and the Ontario Cyber Security Framework/Regulation, coordinating evidence collection, control testing, and gap remediation
Integrate cyber governance, risk, and compliance activities with other hospital risk management and advisory functions, including Enterprise Risk Management, Privacy, Legal, and Internal Audit, to ensure a coordinated approach to risk, incident response, and regulatory obligations
Prepare and present risk and compliance reporting for various committees, senior leadership, and internal/external auditors
Lead third-party risk assessments from a governance perspective, including privacy and contractual risk considerations, in partnership with Procurement, Privacy, and Legal
Own and mature the cyber threat and vulnerability risk management program, including threat intelligence, threat management tools and risk-mitigation processes
Direct prioritization, tracking, and reporting of vulnerability and threat remediation across endpoints, servers, network, and cloud/SaaS environments
Own selection, configuration, and lifecycle management of risk management tooling (e.g., GRC platform, vulnerability management, threat intelligence feeds)
Lead risk assessments for new systems, vendors, and technology changes, and maintain associated risk treatment plans
Conduct direct day-to-day security operations, including SIEM/SOC monitoring, detection, and incident response, delivered through internal staff and managed security service providers
Own the incident response process end-to-end: triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident/lessons-learned review
Direct endpoint security strategy (EDR/anti-malware, hardening baselines) and identity/access security operations, including Cloud Identity Services federation, Epic EHR access, and Microsoft 365/Entra ID security
Coordinate vendor-delivered assessments (penetration tests, tabletop exercises) and ensure findings are integrated into the risk register
Supervise direct reports (e.g., Cyber Security Analyst and IAM/Operations Analyst), including performance management, coaching, and development planning
Perform other duties consistent with the job classification as required

Job Requirements

7 years of related experience in a cybersecurity leadership position
College Diploma or bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Security, or a related technical field

Preferred

Previous experience in a clinical or hospital environment

Skills and Knowledge
